priceNote: Platina 110 H-Gear also sold (around ৳1,40,000).
tagline: The softest-riding 100cc in Bangladesh for people who just want to get there cheaply.
feel: Plush, long-travel suspension and a long padded seat soak up broken Dhaka and village roads better than most commuters. Engine is relaxed up to 60 km/h and runs out of breath past 75.
quirks: Only 4 gears so it buzzes at highway speeds; drum brakes feel weak with a pillion; tube-type tyres on the BD ES variant mean roadside puncture fixes; build quality of plastics and switchgear is basic.
braking: Drum front and rear with combined braking is adequate for 50-60 km/h city use but needs planning on the highway.
mechanicNote: Any roadside mechanic in Bangladesh can service it and parts are sold in every bazaar; Uttara Motors service points cover all districts.
pros: Most comfortable ride in the 100cc class

tagline: Cheapest new Bajaj you can buy — a no-frills workhorse.
feel: Light, simple and forgiving; it feels like a tool rather than a toy. Fine at city speeds, strained beyond 70 km/h.
quirks: Very basic seat and suspension; vibration through the pegs at higher rpm; tube-type tyres; minimal features and dated looks hurt resale.
braking: Plain drums at both ends without any combined system, so stopping distances are long when loaded.
mechanicNote: Shares most hardware with the Platina, so every local mechanic knows it and parts are dirt cheap.
pros: Lowest purchase price in the Bajaj range

priceNote: Discover 110 Disc ৳1,49,600.
tagline: A 125 that rides like a comfy 100 — practical, but out-shined by newer rivals.
feel: Smooth, torquey low end makes it easy in stop-go traffic and it cruises more calmly than a 100cc. Suspension is on the soft, comfortable side.
quirks: Dated design next to the Raider and Glamour X; some owners report vibration in handlebar above 80 km/h and carb tuning drift after a few thousand km; resale lags Hero/Honda 125s.
braking: Front disc gives decent bite for a commuter; rear drum is mushy.
mechanicNote: Simple carb engine that local mechanics fix easily; Bajaj parts are the cheapest and most available in BD.

tagline: The NS look and perimeter frame for 125cc money.
feel: Feels like a big bike: planted, sharp handling and a sporty riding position. The 125 engine needs to be revved, so it's lively rather than fast.
quirks: Heavy for a 125 (144 kg), so mileage is closer to a 150; thin tyres look undersized for the frame; engine heat and a firm ride over potholes; weak low-end pull with a pillion.
braking: Front disc is strong for the weight but there is no ABS or CBS, so panic stops on wet roads need care.
mechanicNote: Shares many parts with the old NS160/NS200 family; Pulsar-savvy mechanics are common, but 4-valve top-end work is best left to Uttara or experienced shops.
bestFor: Young first-time riders wanting sporty looks

priceNote: Single Disc ABS ৳2,10,000; Twin Disc ৳2,17,000; Twin Disc ABS ৳2,31,100.
tagline: The bike every mechanic in Bangladesh already knows inside out.
feel: Familiar, torquey and comfortable, with a big 15 L tank and an upright seat that suits long rides with a pillion. Feels old-school next to newer 160s.
quirks: Engine gets buzzy above 90 km/h; heats up in long Dhaka jams; dated platform with twin rear shocks; base variant has no ABS; some owners complain of DTS-i spark plug and carb tuning needs.
braking: Front disc is adequate; ABS variants are worth the small premium for highway use.
mechanicNote: Probably the best-supported 150cc in BD: every bazaar mechanic and parts shop stocks Pulsar 150 parts, often in cheap aftermarket versions too.

priceNote: Base N160 ৳2,37,000; Twin Disc Carburetor ৳2,42,600; Dual ABS with gold USD fork ৳2,88,000. Official Bajaj BD blog listed ৳2,79,500 in Jan 2025.
tagline: The sensible modern 160 — dual-channel ABS and Pulsar running costs.
feel: Stable, planted and comfortable, with a smooth, torquey engine that pulls cleanly from low revs. Feels more grown-up than an Apache but heavier in tight traffic.
quirks: At ~152 kg it's one of the heaviest 160s, which shows when filtering and pushing in parking; engine heat on thighs in long jams; some owners report rear brake/ABS feeling over-sensitive and mileage dropping under 40 in heavy Dhaka traffic.
braking: Twin discs with dual-channel ABS give the best-in-class safety at this price.
mechanicNote: Uttara Motors service centres handle FI and ABS diagnostics; general mechanics are comfortable with routine work, and Pulsar parts are widely stocked.

tagline: The only affordable cruiser in Bangladesh — laid-back and low.
feel: Low seat, feet-forward pegs and a wide handlebar make it relaxing on straight roads and easy for short riders to flat-foot. Slow-steering compared with street bikes.
quirks: Feet-forward pegs are awkward in stop-go Dhaka traffic and over speed breakers; low ground clearance scrapes on badly built bumps; heavy and slow for its price; rear drum only; cruiser look divides opinion and narrows resale buyers.
braking: Single-channel ABS front disc gives confidence, but the rear drum is weak.
mechanicNote: Engine is a Pulsar-family unit, so mechanics can handle it, but some cruiser-specific body and chassis parts are dealer-only.

priceNote: N250 Fi ABS with USD fork ৳3,60,000. Official Bajaj BD blog listed ৳3,39,999 earlier.
tagline: The cheapest real 250 in Bangladesh — torque for days, Pulsar running costs.
feel: Big mid-range torque makes overtaking on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway effortless and it cruises at 100 km/h without strain. Feels heavy and warm in city crawl.
quirks: Only 5 gears, so it revs higher than ideal on long highway stretches; strong engine heat in Dhaka jams; 162+ kg is tiring to filter and push; some owners note tank-area vibration around 7,000 rpm.
braking: Twin discs with dual-channel ABS are strong and predictable.
mechanicNote: Routine service is straightforward but FI/ABS diagnostics and engine internals are best done at Uttara Motors; some 250-specific parts are not stocked outside major cities.
cons: Heavy and hot in city traffic

priceNote: Newer F250 listed at ৳3,65,100 on bikebd.
tagline: The N250's half-faired tourer twin — wind protection for the highway crowd.
feel: Same punchy 250 engine as the N250 with a half-fairing that takes wind off the chest at 90-110 km/h. Upright bars keep it comfortable rather than sporty.
quirks: Fairing adds weight and makes it even clumsier in Dhaka traffic; heat trapped around the legs; mirrors and fairing panels are expensive dealer-only parts if dropped; 5-speed gearbox.
braking: Dual-channel ABS twin discs, strong and well-calibrated.
mechanicNote: Mechanical parts shared with the N250; fairing panels, headlamp and mounts are dealer-only and can take time to arrive outside Dhaka.
cons: Costly fairing parts after a fall
bestFor: Riders wanting a faired 250 on a budget

priceNote: Metro Plus RE Disc ৳1,31,999.
tagline: TVS's go-to 110 for Bangladeshi commuters and ride-share riders.
feel: Light, easy clutch and smooth low-end make it effortless in traffic. The long seat is reasonably comfy for two.
quirks: Only 4 gears; feels strained above 75 km/h; front drum is weak with a pillion; plastics and paint age quickly in sun and rain.
braking: Drum brakes on the base model are enough for city speeds; the RE Disc variant is worth it for highway use.
mechanicNote: TVS has a wide dealer and service network and the engine is simple enough for any local mechanic; parts are common in most district towns.

tagline: A comfortable, rural-friendly 110 with a long, plush seat.
feel: 18-inch wheels and a long, well-padded seat make it settle over bad rural roads. Engine is smooth and relaxed at commuting speeds.
quirks: Chrome-heavy styling isn't to everyone's taste; only 4 gears; drum brakes; resale is weaker than Hero commuters.
braking: Drum brakes with TVS SBT combined braking are fine for town speeds.
mechanicNote: Shares its 110 engine family with the Metro Plus, so local mechanics are comfortable and parts are easy to find.

tagline: Budget 125 with a front disc for not much more than a 110.
feel: Light and peppy for a 125, easy to thread through traffic and comfortable enough for daily rides.
quirks: Less known than the Raider, so resale and buyer demand are weaker; build and switchgear are basic; owners report vibration at higher revs.
braking: Front disc gives better bite than drum commuters; no CBS or ABS.
mechanicNote: Simple carb engine that local mechanics can handle, but some body parts are TVS dealer-only.

tagline: The sportiest-feeling 125 commuter — quick, light and frugal.
feel: Peppy, light and eager, with the quickest acceleration among 125 commuters and a sharp chassis that loves Dhaka gaps. Monoshock rides firm but controlled.
quirks: 10 L tank is small for highway runs; some owners report vibration above 80 km/h and a hard seat on long rides; pillion seat is short; split seat makes carrying loads awkward.
braking: Front disc with SBT combined braking is confidence-inspiring for a commuter.
mechanicNote: Wide TVS service network; local mechanics handle it well, though the 3-valve head and digital meter are best handled at authorised workshops.
pros: Strong real mileage for its pace

tagline: Light, flickable Apache handling at the price of a Pulsar 150.
feel: Light and agile with quick steering that makes it one of the best bikes for Dhaka gap-filling. Sporty but not tiring.
quirks: Firm rear suspension and a small, hard pillion seat; air-cooled engine heats up in long jams; vibrations creep in above 90 km/h; rear tyre is narrow.
braking: Front disc is sharp; the base refresh lacks ABS, so pick the ABS variant if budget allows.
mechanicNote: One of the most common 160s in BD — local mechanics know it well and parts are widely stocked.

priceNote: Base 4V ৳2,19,900; Fi version ৳2,74,900.
tagline: The enthusiast's 160 — sharp handling and a revvy engine.
feel: Rev-happy oil-cooled engine and a sharp chassis make it the most fun 160 to ride hard. Stable on highways, eager in town.
quirks: Real mileage is in the high-30s in Dhaka traffic; pillion seat is small and high; carb version can feel rough under 3,000 rpm in top gears; rear-only ABS is absent (single-channel front only).
braking: Front single-channel ABS with rear disc gives strong, controllable stops.
mechanicNote: TVS dealer network is strong in major cities; routine work is fine at local shops, but 4-valve top-end and ABS issues should go to TVS service.

tagline: The sporty scooter — quick, feature-rich and gearless.
feel: Quick off the line and easy to dart through traffic with no clutch to work. Feels peppy for a scooter, but 12-inch wheels get unsettled on broken roads.
quirks: Small 12-inch wheels crash into Dhaka potholes and waterlogged ruts; small 5.8 L tank; mileage is worse than geared 125s; low ground clearance on speed breakers.
braking: Front disc is good for a scooter; there is no ABS.
mechanicNote: Fewer roadside mechanics understand CVT scooters well, so belt and roller service is best at TVS centres.
pros: No clutch, very easy in traffic

parts.name: Chain & sprocket set
parts.note: CVT scooter: price shown is drive belt (no chain)

tagline: The most reliable, best-resale commuter you can buy.
feel: Smooth, quiet and almost unbreakable. It's not exciting but it starts every morning and sips fuel.
quirks: Drum brakes feel weak at speed; skinny 2.75-section tyres skate in the wet; only 4 gears; feels underpowered with a pillion on flyovers.
braking: Drums front and rear (IBS on i3S variant) — adequate only at commuter speeds.
mechanicNote: Every mechanic in BD knows the Splendor engine; parts are cheap and everywhere, and Hero's network is wide.

priceNote: HF Deluxe i3S ৳1,16,500.
tagline: Splendor's engine at the lowest Hero price.
feel: Same frugal, smooth 97cc engine as the Splendor in a lighter, simpler package. Easy and unintimidating.
quirks: Very basic seat and suspension; drum brakes; skinny tyres; looks budget.
braking: Drums at both ends — fine for town, weak on highways.
mechanicNote: Shares Splendor mechanicals, so any mechanic can fix it and parts are cheap everywhere.

priceNote: Launched at ৳1,66,000 (intro offer ৳1,63,000). Older Glamour i3S ৳1,50,000.
tagline: The most high-tech 125 commuter in BD — cruise control and ride modes.
feel: Smooth, refined and comfortable, with a calm ride and a family-friendly seat. Cruise control and ride-by-wire make highway stretches relaxed.
quirks: Ride-by-wire, cruise control and TFT are new territory for local mechanics; electrical/sensor repairs mean dealer visits; costs more than conventional 125s.
braking: Front disc with Hero's integrated braking (IBS) feels secure for a commuter.
mechanicNote: Routine service is easy, but FI and ride-by-wire electronics need HMCL Niloy service centres; long-term electronics reliability is still unproven.

tagline: A 125 that looks like a 160 — and has ABS.
feel: Sporty stance with a fat rear tyre and planted feel; quick off the line and efficient. Feels bigger than it is.
quirks: Split seat leaves pillion with a small perch; 10 L tank limits highway range; at 136 kg it's heavier than other 125s; firm monoshock on rough roads.
braking: Front disc with single-channel ABS is a real safety plus in the 125 class.
mechanicNote: FI system and ABS need Hero service tools; routine work is easy and Hero parts are widely available.
pros: Sporty looks with fat rear tyre

priceNote: Dual Disc ৳1,96,000; Hunk 150R Xtec ৳2,15,000.
tagline: Hero's comfortable, no-drama 150 built for Bangladesh.
feel: Calm, comfortable and stable with a roomy seat. Power is modest for a 150, but it's smooth and easy to live with.
quirks: Down on power versus Pulsar 150 and Apache 160; carburetted; resale weaker than Pulsar/Apache; some owners report weak headlight on older units.
braking: Twin discs with single-channel ABS give good control.
mechanicNote: Simple air-cooled carb engine that local mechanics handle; Hero parts are common, though some Hunk-specific body parts are dealer-only.

priceNote: Newer Xtreme 160R 4V with dual-channel ABS ৳2,50,000; 2V Thriller 160R Refresh from ৳2,00,000.
tagline: USD fork, FI and 4 valves for less than an Apache 4V ABS.
feel: Light, quick and well-balanced, with a USD fork that feels planted on corners. Engine is punchy in the mid-range.
quirks: Owners report electrical glitches (headlight/indicator, meter) and occasional parts delays at dealers; small pillion seat; resale weaker than Apache/Pulsar.
braking: Front single-channel ABS with rear disc gives confident stops.
mechanicNote: FI and 4V engine are best serviced at HMCL Niloy centres; local mechanics are less familiar and some parts are dealer-only with waiting times.
pros: USD fork and FI at this price

priceNote: XPulse 200 4V Pro ৳3,65,000.
tagline: The only real budget adventure bike in Bangladesh.
feel: Long-travel suspension shrugs off broken roads, potholes and village tracks; tall, upright and comfortable. Engine is torquey but runs out of steam on fast highways.
quirks: Tube-type spoked tyres mean punctures are messier; tall seat is hard for shorter riders in traffic; buzzy above 90 km/h with only 5 gears; dealer-only parts sometimes slow to arrive.
braking: Single-channel ABS (with off-road rear-ABS-off mode) works well but the front disc feels soft.
mechanicNote: FI and adventure-specific parts need HMCL Niloy centres; local mechanics handle basics but long-travel suspension work is dealer territory.
pros: Unmatched for bad roads and off-road

tagline: A full-faired, liquid-cooled, 6-speed sport-tourer at a sub-5-lakh price.
feel: Smooth, refined liquid-cooled engine with a 6th gear that makes 100-110 km/h cruising relaxed. Sporty but not aggressive ergonomics.
quirks: Pricey and heavy; fairing parts are expensive dealer-only after a fall; liquid cooling, FI and ABS need dealer service; resale is uncertain as it is newer and niche.
braking: Dual-channel ABS with twin discs is strong and predictable.
mechanicNote: Few local mechanics are familiar with liquid-cooled, FI Hero engines; plan on HMCL Niloy service and wait times for fairing/body parts.

priceNote: Xoom 110 ৳1,90,000; Maestro Edge 110 Xtec ৳1,77,000; Pleasure ৳1,65,000.
tagline: A sporty 125 scooter with bigger 14-inch wheels for Bangladeshi roads.
feel: Quick and stable, with 14-inch wheels that handle potholes better than 12-inch rivals. Effortless in Dhaka stop-go.
quirks: Small 5.3 L tank; FI and electronics need dealer service; under-seat storage is modest; higher price than geared 125s.
braking: Front disc with CBS gives balanced stops.
mechanicNote: CVT and FI work is dealer territory; fewer roadside mechanics are confident with scooters.

parts.name: Chain & sprocket set
parts.note: CVT scooter: price shown is drive belt (no chain)

priceNote: Shine 100 DX (newer styling, digital meter) ৳1,17,000. Current refreshed model launched by BHL on 16 Nov 2025.
tagline: The cheapest way into a Honda badge, and it'll outlive your loan.
feel: Light, upright and completely unintimidating; the FI motor is smooth and pulls cleanly from low revs, but anything past 60 km/h feels like work.
quirks: Only 4 gears and 7 PS, so overtaking buses on the Dhaka-Mawa or Dhaka-Aricha highway takes planning. Drum brakes at both ends feel wooden when loaded with a pillion. Thin seat foam gets tiring after an hour.
braking: CBS drum brakes are adequate at commuter speeds but need a firm squeeze and fade on long downhill or loaded stops.
mechanicNote: BHL dealers are everywhere and any roadside mechanic can service the engine; the FI system needs a dealer scan tool if a sensor fails, which is rare.
pros: Tubeless tyres and CBS as standard
Light and easy for new riders

tagline: A no-drama 110 for people who just want to get to work.
feel: Soft, relaxed and easy to trickle through traffic; the carbureted engine is smooth but runs out of breath around 70 km/h.
quirks: Carburetor needs periodic cleaning/tuning, especially after bad fuel. Styling is plain and dated. Only 4 gears; vibrations creep in at 70+ km/h.
braking: Drum-drum CBS stops predictably in city traffic but lacks bite for emergency stops at speed.
mechanicNote: Simple HET carb engine that every mechanic in Bangladesh knows; BHL dealer service is cheap and parts are stocked nationwide.
pros: Simple carb engine anyone can tune

priceNote: Drum variant also listed by BHL; disc CBS is the common pick.
tagline: The 110 that looks a bit more grown-up than it is.
feel: Planted on 18-inch wheels with a decent seat; gentle, smooth power that's happiest between 30 and 60 km/h.
quirks: Carb engine can hesitate on cold mornings and after cheap petrol. Front disc is nice but the rear drum locks easily on wet roads. Still only 4 gears.
braking: Front disc with CBS gives noticeably better stopping than drum-only 110s, though the rear drum feels vague.
mechanicNote: BHL dealer network covers every district; the engine is the same family as Dream/older Livo so local mechanics handle it easily.
pros: Good ground clearance for broken roads

priceNote: Refreshed SP125 introduced Feb 2026; first BHL 125 with PGM-FI (BS-VI) since Nov 2023.
tagline: The smartest-money 125 in Honda's showroom.
feel: Refined, quiet FI engine with a slick 5-speed; relaxed at 70-80 km/h and very frugal in stop-go traffic.
quirks: Narrow 80-section rear tyre feels nervous on wet tarmac and highway crosswinds. Rear suspension is firm with a pillion on potholed roads. Digital meter is hard to read in direct sun.
braking: Front disc with CBS is confidence-inspiring for a commuter but has no ABS.
mechanicNote: FI makes it slightly more dealer-dependent than carb bikes, but basic servicing is simple and BHL parts are widely stocked.
bestFor: Office commuters doing 40+ km a day

priceNote: Single-disc variant ৳1,99,000 (some dealers quote ৳1,97,000).
tagline: A 160 for people who want commuter manners with highway legs.
feel: Calm, torquey low-rev pull and a neutral, upright riding position; it never feels sporty, but it's genuinely comfortable all day.
quirks: Low-revving tune means it flattens out above 100 km/h. Front tyre is narrow for a 160. Styling is commuter-plain, which some buyers dislike for the price.
braking: Single-channel front ABS with discs at both ends gives safe, predictable stops; the rear can still lock.
mechanicNote: Shares its engine family with the X-Blade/Unicorn 160, so dealers and many experienced local mechanics know it well.

priceNote: Listed ৳2,40,000; Oct 2026 'Dey Goal' campaign price ৳2,36,000 and some listings show ৳2,35,000.
tagline: Sharp-looking Honda 160 that rides like a sensible one.
feel: Easy, linear power and light steering; aggressive styling but the ride is calm and predictable rather than sporty.
quirks: Narrow 80-section front tyre looks odd and limits grip under hard braking. Pillion seat is short and high. Resale lags behind FZS/Gixxer in the used market.
braking: Front single-channel ABS with dual discs gives reassuring stops in Dhaka traffic.
mechanicNote: Common BHL engine; dealer servicing is straightforward and spares are stocked, local mechanics are comfortable with it.
pros: Front ABS at a fair price

priceNote: Grey colour ৳2,79,000; Oct 2026 'Dey Goal' offer ৳2,81,000 (৳8,000 cashback).
tagline: The most powerful bike you can buy within BD's old 165cc thinking, now with Honda polish.
feel: Punchy mid-range and a stiff, planted chassis with the USD fork; quick steering makes it fun weaving through Dhaka traffic.
quirks: Rear suspension is hard and pillions complain on bad roads. Some owners report buzzing through the bars above 85-90 km/h and back fatigue on long rides. Rear brake can squeal.
braking: Petal discs with single-channel ABS give strong, well-controlled stops; one of the better-braking bikes in its price band.
mechanicNote: Dealer-serviced by most owners; local mechanics handle routine work, but USD fork servicing and FI diagnostics are best left to BHL workshops.

priceNote: Launched by BHL 20 Dec 2025; successor to the CB200X concept.
tagline: An upright, ABS-everything tourer for broken roads, not a real off-roader.
feel: Hornet 2.0 engine in a taller, more relaxed package; comfortable on long highway stints and smooth over potholes.
quirks: Despite the ADV styling it uses 17-inch road tyres and only 167mm clearance, so it's not for mud or sand. Taller seat may be tricky for short riders in stop-go jams. Still new in BD, so long-term owner data is limited.
braking: Dual-channel ABS plus slipper clutch make it the safest-braking Honda in BD under ৳6 lakh.
mechanicNote: Engine is shared with the Hornet 2.0 so dealers know it, but TFT, HSTC (traction control) and body panels are dealer-only for now.
bestFor: Riders who want max safety tech

priceNote: Indonesian-built CBR150R sold by BHL; price has climbed from ৳5,38,000 (2021 launch).
tagline: Honda's racer-replica for those who don't want an R15.
feel: Smooth, revvy DOHC engine that loves the top end; the low clip-ons and firm suspension make it a weekend toy more than a commuter.
quirks: Very expensive for 17 PS; an R15 V4 offers more tech for less. Forward-leaning riding position gets painful in Dhaka jams and heat builds up from the radiator. Pillion seat is a perch.
braking: Dual-channel ABS with a strong front disc gives excellent, confidence-inspiring braking.
mechanicNote: Liquid-cooled DOHC needs a dealer or a sport-bike specialist; fairing panels and USD fork parts are dealer-only and slow to arrive.
bestFor: Honda loyalists wanting a sport bike

tagline: Twist-and-go Honda for short city hops.
feel: Light, nimble and genuinely easy in jams; small 10-inch wheels make it twitchy over potholes and speed-breakers.
quirks: Expensive for a 110 carb scooter in BD. Small 10-inch wheels crash into potholes and waterlogged roads. Tiny under-seat storage and small 5.3L tank. Not happy on highways.
braking: Drum-drum CBS is fine at city speeds but doesn't inspire confidence in sudden stops.
mechanicNote: Honda dealers service it routinely, but fewer roadside mechanics understand CVT belts/rollers than geared bikes.

parts.name: Chain & sprocket set
parts.note: No chain on a CVT scooter; figure is the drive belt replacement instead

parts.name: Clutch plate set
parts.note: CVT centrifugal clutch shoes, not a manual clutch plate set

tagline: Yamaha's frugal 125 for people who count every litre.
feel: Torquey low down and very relaxed; the gearing is tall so it cruises smoothly at 60-70 km/h.
quirks: Only 4 gears on a 125. Small 7.6L tank means frequent pump stops. Thin 2.75 front tyre. Styling feels dated next to SP125.
braking: Front disc with Yamaha UBS (combined) gives safe, linked stops but no ABS.
mechanicNote: ACI dealer network is smaller than Honda's but the carb engine is simple for local mechanics; parts are easy in cities, slower in villages.

priceNote: Eid 2026 offer price ৳2,65,000.
tagline: The half-faired FZ for riders who do highway runs every month.
feel: FZ chassis with a fairing that cuts wind on highways; upright, comfy seat and a soft, relaxed engine.
quirks: Old V2-generation engine with no ABS and a rear drum at this price. Heavier front end feels slower in tight traffic than the FZS. Feels dated next to newer 150-160s.
braking: Front disc only and no ABS; adequate but behind the times at ৳2.7 lakh.
mechanicNote: Shares most mechanicals with the FZS V2, one of the most familiar bikes to BD mechanics; ACI parts are easy to source.

priceNote: Older FZS V3 ABS ~৳2,58,500-2,71,000 and FZS V2 ~৳2,29,000 still sold by ACI (May 2026 list).
tagline: The default answer to 'which 150cc should I buy?' in Bangladesh.
feel: Low-revving, torquey and very easy; fat rear tyre and upright bars make it stable and friendly in traffic.
quirks: Power is modest at 12.4 PS, so it runs out of steam above 100 km/h. Some owners find the seat hard after an hour. Expensive compared with similar-power Indian 150s.
braking: Single-channel front ABS with rear disc gives safe, predictable braking.
mechanicNote: FZ family is the most familiar 150cc platform for BD mechanics after Pulsar; ACI and the grey market both stock parts.
cons: Seat gets hard on long rides

priceNote: Launch price ৳3,49,500 (pre-booking offer ৳3,43,500); BD's first hybrid motorcycle.
tagline: An FZS that switches itself off at Dhaka signals.
feel: Rides exactly like the FZS V4, but silent starts and stop-start make crawling through jams calmer; TFT with navigation is a real upgrade.
quirks: Not a true hybrid: the motor-generator only assists starts/acceleration, so mileage gains are modest (a few kmpl in heavy traffic). ৳50k+ premium over the V4. Stop-start system and TFT are new to local mechanics.
braking: Same single-channel ABS and dual discs as the FZS V4: safe and predictable.
mechanicNote: Engine and chassis are standard FZ, but the SMG/stop-start electrics and TFT should only be touched by ACI service centres.
bestFor: Daily Dhaka commute in heavy traffic

priceNote: Matt Titan colour offer ৳2,95,000; some colours ৳2,99,500 (May 2026).
tagline: An FZ in neo-retro clothes with a comfier seat.
feel: Upright, wide bars and a flat, plush seat make it the comfiest FZ; same easy low-rev engine.
quirks: It looks like a scrambler but it's a road bike with road tyres. Smaller 10L tank than the FZS. Round LED headlamp throw is weaker than expected on dark highways.
braking: Single-channel ABS up front with discs at both ends; dependable.
mechanicNote: Mechanically an FZS, so any FZ-savvy mechanic can work on it; body parts are ACI-only.

priceNote: May 2026 offer price ৳3,98,000 after ৳12,000 discount shown elsewhere; prices vary by dealer stock.
tagline: The relaxed 250 for highway cruising without the sport-bike pain.
feel: Big, grunty low-end and a calm, upright stance; feels like a heavier, stronger FZ rather than a sporty 250.
quirks: Only 5 gears, so it revs higher than you'd like at 100+ km/h. Air-cooled engine gets hot in summer jams. Ageing design with older tech than Gixxer 250. Weak used-market demand.
braking: Dual-channel ABS makes it one of the safest Yamahas under ৳4 lakh.
mechanicNote: Simple air-cooled SOHC engine, but 250cc parts are mostly at ACI dealers; fewer local mechanics have worked on one.

tagline: Bangladesh's dream bike: the 150cc sport-bike benchmark.
feel: VVA engine pulls hard from mid-range to the 10k+ redline; razor-sharp handling and a slick quickshifter-ready gearbox (quickshifter on R15M).
quirks: Aggressive riding position is tiring in Dhaka jams and the radiator fan pumps heat onto your legs. Pillion seat is tiny. Big theft target, so owners spend on locks/trackers. Priced like a 300cc bike due to BD import duty.
braking: Dual-channel ABS with a strong front disc; excellent and predictable.
mechanicNote: Many specialist sport-bike mechanics in Dhaka know R15s well, but VVA/FI diagnostics and fairing parts are best sourced from ACI.
pros: Dual ABS, USD fork, traction control

priceNote: Dark Knight ৳5,25,000; Racing Blue ~৳5,21,000 (May 2026). Indonesian V3 (USD fork) listed ~৳5,50,000.
tagline: R15 thrills for ~৳85k less than the V4.
feel: Same VVA rush as the V4 with slightly softer, more forgiving conventional forks; still a committed sport riding position.
quirks: Conventional fork and older styling; no traction control. Heat on legs in traffic. Being phased out globally, so future stock could dry up.
braking: Dual-channel ABS gives strong, safe stopping.
mechanicNote: The most familiar R15 to BD sport-bike mechanics; parts widely available through ACI and the open market.

priceNote: Older MT-15 (V1) stock still listed at ৳4,60,000.
tagline: R15 engine, upright bars, wheelie-happy attitude.
feel: Punchy, revvy and light-steering; much easier in city traffic than the R15 thanks to upright bars.
quirks: No wind protection, so highway speeds above 100 km/h are tiring. Pillion seat is small and high. Short 10L tank. Expensive vs the R15 V3 for similar engine.
braking: USD fork and dual-channel ABS give sharp, safe braking.
mechanicNote: Shares the R15's mechanicals so specialist mechanics know it; USD fork and electronics best handled at ACI.

priceNote: Launched by ACI on 20 March (price unchanged since launch per BikeBD).
tagline: Neo-retro looks with an R15 heart.
feel: Light, flickable and upright, with the R15's revvy VVA motor; feels premium and playful.
quirks: Indonesian-built and pricey; many units lack ABS. Retro-specific parts (tank, lights, seat) are dealer-only and slow. Small 10L tank.
braking: Discs at both ends bite well but check the unit for ABS; many BD units don't have it.
mechanicNote: Engine shared with R15/MT-15 so mechanics are comfortable; cosmetic and chassis parts are dealer-only.

priceNote: BikeBD also lists a Ray ZR Street Rally variant at ৳2,25,000; check dealer for current hybrid vs non-hybrid stock.
tagline: A light, sporty 125 scooter for jam-heavy Dhaka.
feel: Very light at 99 kg and quick off the line thanks to hybrid assist; easy to filter through traffic.
quirks: Small 5.2L tank. Small rear wheel and low 145mm clearance scrape on speed-breakers and flooded roads. Expensive for a 125 scooter. Few local mechanics understand the hybrid starter-generator.
braking: Front disc with UBS combined braking stops well for a light scooter.
mechanicNote: ACI service centres handle it; basic CVT servicing is fine at scooter specialists, but the hybrid electrics are dealer-only.

parts.note: No chain on a CVT scooter; figure is the drive belt replacement instead

parts.name: Clutch plate set
parts.note: CVT centrifugal clutch shoes, not a manual clutch plate set

priceNote: Launched Nov 2023 at ৳5,30,000.
tagline: A maxi-scooter with R15 tech for people who hate shifting.
feel: Quick off the line and stable at 90-100 km/h on 14-inch wheels; the VVA motor makes it feel like a 150cc bike without the clutch.
quirks: Very expensive for a scooter in BD. Only 5.5L tank so highway range is short. Low clearance scrapes on speed-breakers. Few mechanics outside ACI understand the liquid-cooled VVA CVT.
braking: Front single-channel ABS gives safe stops, but the rear drum is weak.
mechanicNote: Dealer-dependent: CVT, VVA and liquid cooling need ACI service; scooter-specific parts can take time.

parts.name: Chain & sprocket set
parts.note: No chain on a CVT scooter; figure is the drive belt replacement instead

parts.name: Clutch plate set
parts.note: CVT centrifugal clutch shoes, not a manual clutch plate set

tagline: The cheapest Suzuki, and a simple, tough 110.
feel: Light, plain and easy; a bit peppier than most 100s with a soft ride over broken roads.
quirks: Drum brakes with no CBS. Dated design and basic analogue cluster. Resale weaker than Honda 110s. Rancon dealer coverage thins out in rural areas.
braking: Drum-drum without CBS; adequate in the city but needs care in the wet.
mechanicNote: Simple carb engine local mechanics can handle; Suzuki-specific parts are mostly at Rancon dealers outside big cities.

priceNote: Launched July 2020 at ৳1,34,950.
tagline: A big-tank 125 that makes a lot of sense on paper.
feel: Revvy rather than torquey, with a roomy seat; stable at 70-80 km/h with a solid, heavier feel than other 125s.
quirks: Peaky engine needs revs, so stop-go mileage drops. Heavier than rivals at 126 kg. Low brand recognition hurts resale. Parts outside Rancon dealers can be hard to find.
braking: Big 290mm front disc bites well, though there's no CBS or ABS.
mechanicNote: Simple carb engine, but it isn't a common platform, so model-specific parts often mean a trip to a Rancon dealer.

priceNote: Official 'start from' price; BikeBD lists ৳2,05,950 (same as Gixxer Classic Matt). Carb Disc ৳2,37,950.
tagline: The cheapest proper 150 with a fat tyre and a punchy engine.
feel: Lively, light and torquey low down; the old-generation carb Gixxer is still one of the most fun budget 150s in town.
quirks: Carb engine with no ABS and a rear drum. Older styling. Engine gets buzzy above 90 km/h. Fit and finish feels budget.
braking: Front disc only and no ABS; fine for city use but basic.
mechanicNote: Carb Gixxer is extremely familiar to BD mechanics; parts are cheap and found everywhere.

priceNote: Gixxer FI Disc (no ABS) ৳2,51,950. Rancon news has older prices (FI ABS ৳2,66,950).
tagline: The FZS rival with sharper looks and a peppier engine.
feel: Smooth, eager FI engine, light steering and a planted feel; more playful than the FZS.
quirks: Some owners report a rattly/creaky body and electrical niggles. Split seat is firm for pillions. Resale slightly below the FZS.
braking: Single-channel front ABS with discs at both ends brakes well.
mechanicNote: Gixxer platform is very familiar to BD mechanics; FI diagnostics need a Rancon dealer.

priceNote: Gixxer SF FI Disc (no ABS) ৳3,19,950.
tagline: Full-fairing looks at half the price of an R15.
feel: Comfortable for a faired bike with semi-clip-ons; stable on highways with good wind protection, but it's a 13.6 PS 150, not a racer.
quirks: Looks fast but isn't; performance is the same as the naked Gixxer. Heavier than the naked version. Fairing parts are expensive if dropped.
braking: Front single-channel ABS with dual discs works well.
mechanicNote: Same engine as the Gixxer so mechanics know it; fairing panels mostly through Rancon dealers.
bestFor: Riders who can't stretch to R15

tagline: The best-value 250 in Bangladesh's legal market.
feel: Smooth, refined oil-cooled engine with real highway punch; stable and relaxed at 100-110 km/h.
quirks: Heat on thighs in summer traffic. Heavier than 150s at slow speed. Resale market for 250s is thin. Some report vibrations around 8,000 rpm.
braking: Dual-channel ABS with a big front disc gives strong, safe stopping.
mechanicNote: SOCS oil-cooling is unique to Suzuki; best serviced at Rancon dealers. Local mechanics are still learning 250s.

priceNote: Special Edition also ৳4,29,950 per BikeBD.
tagline: A real 250cc sport-tourer for less than an R15.
feel: Comfortable clip-ons, good wind protection and a refined engine make it a genuine highway tourer; heavy-ish in city traffic.
quirks: Heat and weight in Dhaka jams. Fairing panels expensive and dealer-only. Thin 250cc resale market.
braking: Dual-channel ABS and a big front disc are reassuring at highway speeds.
mechanicNote: Oil-cooled 250 needs Rancon dealer service; fairing and electrical parts are dealer-only.
pros: Cheaper and more powerful than R15 V4

tagline: The lightest, revviest 150 sport bike in BD.
feel: Feather-light with a screaming DOHC engine that wants to live above 9,000 rpm; brilliant on an empty road, frustrating in jams.
quirks: Peaky engine is weak below 7,000 rpm, so city riding means constant gear changes. Skinny 90/80 front tyre. Parts are imported from Indonesia and can take weeks. Smaller fan base than R15 means weaker resale.
braking: Dual-channel ABS with a strong front disc provides confident braking.
mechanicNote: Few mechanics outside Rancon know this Indonesian-built DOHC engine; plan on dealer service and parts waits.

tagline: The comfiest, most sensible family scooter in BD.
feel: Smooth, torquey 125 that pulls cleanly with a pillion; plush seat and roomy floorboard make it family-friendly.
quirks: Priced well above Indian market levels. Small 10-inch rear wheel bumps over potholes. Drum brakes on the CBS variant. Scooter-savvy mechanics are fewer than bike mechanics outside Dhaka.
braking: CBS drum brakes are adequate for city speeds; the disc variant isn't commonly sold here.
mechanicNote: Rancon dealers service it routinely; CVT and FI need a trained mechanic, but it's one of the most familiar scooters in BD.
cons: Small rear wheel on bad roads

priceNote: Rebel Blue/Red/Black dual-channel ABS ৳3,71,500; base Hunter 350 (Retro, single-channel ABS, rear drum) listed at ৳3,46,500. Launched Oct 2024 at ~৳3.4 lakh.
tagline: The cheapest, lightest way into the Royal Enfield thump.
feel: Low-revving, torquey and relaxed — it pulls cleanly from 30 km/h in third and cruises happily at 80-90. Shorter wheelbase and 17-inch wheels make it the most agile RE, but it still feels heavy next to a 150cc.
quirks: 181 kg is a lot when pushing it in a Mirpur parking lot; the engine throws real heat on your thighs in Dhaka jams; firm rear suspension crashes over BD potholes and speed breakers; small 13 L tank for a 350.
braking: Dual-channel ABS with discs at both ends is genuinely good and confidence-inspiring on wet roads.
mechanicNote: Service only at IFAD's RE 3S dealers (mostly Dhaka and a few big cities); local mechanics are still learning the J-series engine, so out-of-Dhaka owners rely on the dealer network.
cons: Limited service network outside big cities

priceNote: Halcyon Green/Black ৳4,32,500; Classic 350 Dark (Gun Metal Grey/Stealth Black) ৳4,47,700; Chrome Red/Bronze ৳4,83,000.
tagline: The bike Bangladeshis waited years to buy officially.
feel: Plush, upright and unhurried — big 19-inch front wheel and soft seat soak up broken roads, and the thump at 80 km/h is the whole point. It is a cruiser in spirit, not a filtering tool.
quirks: 195 kg feels every gram in Dhaka gridlock and when parking; heat off the engine is noticeable in summer; spoked wheels mean tube tyres (punctures are a roadside hassle); the base variant has a rear drum.
braking: Front disc with single-channel ABS is adequate, but the heavy bike needs planning ahead — the rear drum on lower variants is soft.
mechanicNote: Dealer-dependent: IFAD's RE 3S network is small and Dhaka-heavy, and genuine parts mostly come through it. Local mechanics who know the old UCE Classic are not automatically right for the new J-series engine.
pros: Very comfortable for rider and pillion
Strong demand on the used market
cons: Few service centers outside major cities
bestFor: Riders who value style and comfort over agility

priceNote: Single listed variant in BD; launched at ~৳4.1 lakh in Oct 2024.
tagline: Old-school Bullet looks, modern J-series smoothness.
feel: Same smooth 350 as the Classic in a plainer, more traditional body with a flatter long seat. Calm and stable at highway speeds, slow-witted in traffic.
quirks: As heavy as the Classic; spoked wheels with tube tyres; owners note heat on legs in traffic and that the hand-painted pinstripe finish needs care. Some buyers find the Classic better value for slightly more money.
braking: Discs front and rear with dual-channel ABS per the BD listing — stops securely, though weight transfer is noticeable.
mechanicNote: IFAD RE dealers handle service and parts; the network is still small, so plan service visits if you live outside Dhaka/Chattogram.
cons: Close in price to the Classic

priceNote: Stellar ৳4,83,000; Supernova ৳5,08,000. bikebd also lists a base Meteor 350 (Fireball) at ৳4,35,000 but marks it not currently available.
tagline: The most comfortable highway bike you can buy new in Bangladesh under ৳5 lakh.
feel: Feet-forward, low 765 mm seat and a big tank make it a true cruiser — effortless at 90 km/h on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, and the Tripper navigation pod is genuinely useful.
quirks: Feet-forward pegs and wide bars make slow U-turns and lane-splitting awkward; 191 kg plus heat in summer jams; low ground clearance under the exhaust scrapes on steep BD speed breakers with a pillion.
braking: Dual discs with dual-channel ABS — strong and predictable for a heavy cruiser.
mechanicNote: IFAD RE 3S dealers only for proper service and Tripper/electrical issues; local mechanics are rarely familiar with it yet.
pros: Tripper navigation, alloy wheels, tubeless tyres
bestFor: Shorter riders wanting a big bike

priceNote: Indian-made unit ৳3,00,000; European Edition ৳3,70,000. KTM India discontinued the 125s in 2025, so BD availability depends on remaining Runner stock — confirm with dealer.
tagline: Big-bike chassis and KTM badge on a 125cc legal budget.
feel: Premium chassis, USD fork, wide rear tyre and sharp steering — it feels like a much bigger bike than it is. The 125 engine needs revving past 7,000 rpm to make progress.
quirks: Gutless below 6,000 rpm so you're constantly downshifting in traffic; liquid-cooled engine still gets hot in jams; firm seat and tiny pillion perch; KTM's Indian 125 range is discontinued, so long-term parts support depends on Runner.
braking: Bybre disc brakes with ABS are strong and well-modulated for a 125.
mechanicNote: Runner's KTM service points only (a handful, mostly Dhaka); owners on bikebd complain service cost is roughly double a normal bike. Local mechanics avoid the FI/liquid-cooled KTM engine.
cons: Discontinued in India — future parts uncertain

priceNote: Offer price ৳3,70,000 (regular ৳4,43,000) per bikebd. KTM India discontinued the RC 125 in 2025; BD availability depends on remaining Runner stock.
tagline: Full-fairing KTM superbike looks with a 125cc heart.
feel: Committed clip-on riding position and a stiff, precise chassis — great on an empty flyover, tiring in Dhaka traffic. Needs high revs to keep pace with 150-160cc commuters.
quirks: Aggressive wrist-heavy posture tiring in jams; pillion seat is a token perch; heat trapped by fairing in summer; expensive fairing panels if dropped; discontinued in India so long-term parts support is uncertain.
braking: Single-channel ABS (Bosch) with front and rear discs — strong and progressive.
mechanicNote: Runner KTM service points only; fairing removal and FI diagnosis are dealer jobs. Expect noticeably higher service and parts bills than Japanese/Indian 150s.

priceNote: Older Bullet 100 ৳1,06,000; Bullet 100 V2 Matt ৳1,09,000.
tagline: Made-in-Bangladesh 100cc for the tightest budgets.
feel: Light, easy and slow — fine for neighbourhood and town runs, but it runs out of breath above 60-70 km/h and with a pillion.
quirks: Owners report vibration at higher revs, a weak headlight and average brakes; build quality and paint finish below Bajaj/Hero 100s; resale value drops fast.
braking: Front disc is better than drum-only rivals, but overall braking feel is basic.
mechanicNote: Simple Chinese-derived 100cc engine that any roadside mechanic can work on; Runner has one of the widest dealer networks (150+ points), and generic parts fit.

priceNote: Original Knight Rider ৳1,59,000.
tagline: A 150cc look for 125cc money — with local-brand compromises.
feel: Upright and stable with a simple CBF-type engine; acceptable around town but gets breathless and buzzy past 90 km/h.
quirks: Fit-and-finish and switchgear quality well below Japanese/Indian 150s; owners report vibration and electrical niggles; resale is weak — expect a big loss when selling.
braking: Front disc/rear drum without CBS or ABS — adequate at commuter speeds only.
mechanicNote: Runner's large dealer network and the simple carb engine mean most local mechanics can service it; cosmetic/body parts may need the dealer.

priceNote: EFI ৳2,28,000; Carburetor version ৳2,14,000.
tagline: The most power and fairing per taka — if you accept Chinese-bike trade-offs.
feel: Full-faired, liquid-cooled 165 with strong mid-range for the price; comfortable-ish semi-sporty posture and stable on the highway.
quirks: Owners report disappointing mileage (carb version often ~30 km/l), a huge turning radius that hurts U-turns in Dhaka, overheating complaints in jams, chain needing frequent tightening, and a rear shock that is poor with a pillion. Resale is weak.
braking: Disc front and rear with CBS but no ABS — decent bite, but locks up on wet roads under panic braking.
mechanicNote: Rasel Industries' Lifan service points cover major towns; local mechanics can do basic work but liquid cooling and EFI diagnostics are dealer jobs, and some parts (fairings, electricals) can take time to arrive.
pros: Lots of power and features for the money
bestFor: Highway riders on a tight budget

priceNote: 2-valve KPT 150 listed at ৳2,60,000.
tagline: A budget adventure-tourer with dual-channel ABS under ৳3 lakh.
feel: Tall, upright touring posture with a windscreen and roomy seat; the 4-valve liquid-cooled engine is happiest spinning at highway speeds rather than lugging in traffic.
quirks: Owners call the headlamp insufficient for night highway riding; suspension is only moderate on broken roads despite ADV styling; 158 kg and wide bodywork slow you in Dhaka traffic; weak resale like most Chinese bikes.
braking: Twin discs with dual-channel ABS — a real safety advantage at this price.
mechanicNote: Dealer servicing via Rasel Industries' Lifan network recommended; the 4V liquid-cooled EFI engine is unfamiliar to most local mechanics.
pros: Dual-channel ABS at a low price
bestFor: Riders wanting ABS on a budget

priceNote: Offer price ৳3,14,999 (regular ৳3,24,000). Demon GR165RR (dual-channel ABS) ৳3,70,000.
tagline: Thai-built faired 165 with USD forks — lots of show for the money.
feel: Sporty and planted with a USD fork that handles corners well; the liquid-cooled 165 revs freely. Posture is committed and the pillion seat is small.
quirks: No ABS or CBS at this price is a real omission; owners say the USD suspension is harsh on bumpy BD roads; feels heavy and the pillion seat is tiny; small tank limits range; resale and parts depend on a small distributor.
braking: Twin discs without ABS — good bite on dry tarmac but no safety net in rain.
mechanicNote: Speedoz/GPX service is concentrated in Dhaka and a few big cities; local mechanics rarely know the engine, and fairing/electrical parts can be slow to source.
pros: USD fork, LED lights, sporty design
bestFor: Sport-bike looks on a mid budget

priceNote: Da Corsa edition listed at ৳3,59,999 on bikebd's brand page.
tagline: Full-fairing racer styling with dual-channel ABS, priced against the R15.
feel: Proper supersport look and a revvy 4-valve engine that makes its power up top; clip-on posture is sporty and tiring in slow traffic.
quirks: Owners note it is heavy for a 165 (155 kg), the headlamp is weak for night highway use, and there's no traction control; at this price buyers cross-shop the Yamaha R15/Suzuki Gixxer SF with much better resale.
braking: Twin discs with dual-channel ABS — the key upgrade over the GR165R.
mechanicNote: Service and parts through Speedoz/GPX dealers, mostly in Dhaka; fairing and electrical parts are dealer-only.
bestFor: Riders who want something different from R15

tagline: Suzuki-linked Chinese streetfighter with FI, CBS and USD forks under ৳2 lakh.
feel: Smooth, low-vibration air-cooled FI engine with good weight balance; comfortable enough for daily use, competent up to ~110 km/h.
quirks: An 8,000 km owner reported 40-45 km/l but a stiff seat, high pillion seat, and seat height awkward for riders under 5'5"; outside Dhaka the service centres can be poorly equipped and some parts are hard to find.
braking: Disc front and rear with CBS — owners rate stopping power highly for the class.
mechanicNote: Karnaphuli's Haojue network is decent in Dhaka but thinner outside; the engine is simple air-cooled FI, so experienced local mechanics can manage routine work, though FI diagnosis and some parts need the dealer.
pros: FI, CBS and USD fork at a low price
bestFor: Riders wanting features on a budget

tagline: The tech-loaded Chinese premium 155 — keyless, TFT, dual-ABS.
feel: Refined 4-valve liquid-cooled engine, comfortable upright ADV-street posture and a feature list (keyless ignition, TFT, adjustable screen) no Japanese 150 matches.
quirks: Priced near Japanese/Indian ABS 150-160s that hold value far better; small distributor means parts for electronics and body panels can take weeks; owners on forums worry about long-term electrical reliability in BD heat and rain.
braking: Twin discs with dual-channel ABS — excellent for the class.
mechanicNote: Service is essentially dealer-only through Moto Solution BD; very few local mechanics have worked on Zontes engines or electronics.

tagline: The style statement scooter — Italian looks, steel body, premium price.
feel: Solid steel monocoque and smooth CVT make it calm and easy in Dhaka traffic; small wheels and modest power keep it a city machine.
quirks: Expensive for a 125cc scooter; small wheels crash into potholes and feel nervous on rough roads; panels are steel so dents mean costly bodywork; parts and specialist mechanics are limited outside Runner dealers.
braking: Front disc with CBS is adequate for city speeds.
mechanicNote: Runner's Vespa/Aprilia service points handle it; local mechanics can do basic CVT work, but body and trim parts are dealer-only and sometimes back-ordered.

parts.name: Chain & sprocket set
parts.note: CVT scooter — no chain; price is for the drive belt

tagline: A comfortable maxi-style scooter for those who refuse to shift gears.
feel: Plush wide seat, tall screen and easy CVT make it relaxed in traffic and decent for short highway hops; the 160cc engine is smooth but not quick.
quirks: Very expensive for a scooter — the price buys an ABS 150cc motorcycle; 12-inch wheels thud through deep potholes; big body makes lane-splitting harder than on a small scooter; dealer-only parts.
braking: Front disc with single-channel ABS — reassuring for a scooter.
mechanicNote: Service via Runner's Aprilia/Vespa outlets; local mechanics can handle CVT basics but FI and body parts are dealer-only.
pros: Very comfortable rider and pillion seat

parts.name: Chain & sprocket set
parts.note: CVT scooter — no chain; price is for the drive belt

priceNote: Bikroy listings mostly ৳35,000-55,000 for local-used examples; very rough units ~৳20,000, clean Japanese-era bikes can ask more.
tagline: The unkillable pushrod Honda every BD mechanic grew up fixing.
feel: Simple, upright and torquey low down; it plods along all day at 60-70 km/h and shrugs off rough rural roads.
quirks: Drum brakes front and rear are weak by modern standards; 6V-era electrics and dim lights on older units; many have tampered odometers, non-genuine engines or patched papers — check registration carefully; vibrates above 80 km/h.
braking: Drum brakes at both ends — plan stops early, especially with a pillion.
mechanicNote: Every village mechanic knows the CG's OHV engine; generic and Pakistani/Chinese clone parts are cheap and everywhere, though quality varies.

priceNote: Bikroy asks range ৳28,000 (rough) to ৳1,10,000 (restored/modified); fresh-condition examples typically ৳70,000-90,000.
tagline: The two-stroke legend — light, loud and addictive.
feel: Featherweight with an explosive two-stroke punch — it darts through traffic and pulls harder than many 125cc four-strokes, with that unmistakable exhaust note.
quirks: Thirsty and smoky by modern standards, needs 2T oil top-ups; drum brakes are weak for its pace; most units are 25-40 years old with replaced or fake parts; restoration quality varies wildly; some areas see police scrutiny of loud/smoky two-strokes.
braking: Drum brakes front and rear — poor relative to how quickly it accelerates.
mechanicNote: Old-school two-stroke mechanics still exist in most towns and rebuilds are cheap, but genuine Yamaha parts are scarce — most are aftermarket/reproduction.

parts.name: Engine oil change
parts.note: Gearbox oil change; 2T oil is topped up separately

priceNote: Few listings: ৳50,000 for a 2001 local-used unit up to ৳1,55,000 for an original 1992 Japanese example with full papers.
tagline: The bigger-bore RX that two-stroke fans hunt for.
feel: Like the RX100 with extra mid-range shove — light, rev-happy and raw, with the classic two-stroke crackle.
quirks: Rarer than the RX100, so parts are harder and fakes/mismatched engines common; thirsty and smoky; drum brakes; papers on older units often incomplete — verify chassis/engine numbers.
braking: Drum brakes front and rear — inadequate for its acceleration.
mechanicNote: Two-stroke specialists can rebuild it, sharing many parts with the RX100, but model-specific parts are scarce and often reproduction quality.

parts.name: Engine oil change
parts.note: Gearbox oil change; 2T oil is topped up separately

priceNote: Bikroy listings for CBZ / CBZ Xtreme-era bikes mostly ৳40,000-65,000 depending on year and condition.
tagline: The original Indian 150-class 'power bike' — Honda engine, budget used price.
feel: Torquey, long-stroke Honda-derived engine with relaxed gearing; feels sturdy and planted, if dated.
quirks: Most units are 15-25 years old: tired suspension, worn wiring and fading lights are common; bikroy listings often mix up CBZ, CBZ Xtreme and later Hero models, so confirm exactly what you're buying and that papers are valid.
braking: Front disc and rear drum — acceptable for its pace if the disc and pads are in good shape.
mechanicNote: Very familiar to local mechanics, and engine internals share parts with other Hero/Honda models; some body and trim parts are now hard to find.
